en: Of or relating to industry, notably manufacturing.
Produced by such industry.
An enterprise producing tangible goods or providing certain services to industrial companies.
A bond or stock issued by such a company.

industrial.ety: From French industriel. By surface analysis, industry + -al.

ex.en: The Industrial Revolution took place first in England.
ex.ja: 産業革命は最初イギリスに起こった。

ex.en: The town is an industrial community.
ex.ja: その町は産業共同体である。

ex.en: Many people work in industrial towns.
ex.ja: 多くの人々が工業都市で働いている。

note.ja: industry + -al。「産業の・工業の」。

en: United, combined
Done by two or more people or organisations working together.
The point where two components of a structure join, but are still able to rotate.
The point where two components of a structure join rigidly.
To unite by a joint or joints; to fit together; to prepare so as to fit together
To join; to connect; to unite; to combine.

joint.ety:
The noun is from Middle English joynt (attested since the late 13th century), from Old French joint (“joint of the body”) (attested since the 12th century). The adjective (attested since the 15th century) is from Old French jointiz. Both Old French words are from Latin iūnctus, the past participle of iungō. See also join, jugular, junction. Displaced Old English fōg and partially displaced English lith.
The meaning of "building, establishment", especially in connection with shady activities, appeared in Anglo-Irish by 1821 and entered general American English slang by 1877, especially in the s

ex.en: The two companies combined in a joint corporation.
ex.ja: その二つの会社は合併して合弁会社となった。

ex.en: My husband and I have a joint bank account.
ex.ja: 夫と私は共同の銀行口座を持っています。

ex.en: They agreed on a joint statement.
ex.ja: 彼らは共同声明に同意した。

note.ja: ラテン語 iungere（結ぶ）の過去分詞から。結ばれたところ →「関節・つなぎ目」、結ばれた →「共同の」。

en: To stir together.
To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).
The result of mixing two or more substances; a mixture.
The result of combining items normally kept separate.

mix.ety:
From Middle English mixen (attested in past tense as mixed, myxyd), from Old English *mixian, miscian, from Proto-West Germanic *miskijan, from Proto-West Germanic *miskijan (“to mix”), from Proto-Indo-European *miḱ-sḱé-ti, from *meyǵ-, *meyḱ- (“to mix”).
Cognate with Saterland Frisian miskje (“to mix, blend”), Middle Dutch mischen (“to mix”), Low German misken, mischen (“to mix”), Old High German miskian, miskēn (“to mix”) (German mischen), Welsh mysgu (“to mix”), Latin misceō (“mix”), Ancient Greek μῑ́γνῡμῐ (mī́gnūmĭ, “to mix”), Old Church Slavonic мѣсити (měsiti, “to mix”), Lithuanian mišti

ex.en: I don't like to mix business with pleasure.
ex.ja: 仕事と遊びを一緒にするのは、好きではない。

ex.en: Mix three eggs and a cup of sugar.
ex.ja: 卵３個と１カップの砂糖をまぜてください。

ex.en: Don't get mixed up with those people.
ex.ja: あの人たちと関わりあいを持たないようにしなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 mixtus（混ぜられた）から逆成した語。miscere（混ぜる）。「混ぜる」。

en: A building or institution dedicated to the acquisition, conservation, study, exhibition, and educational interpretation of objects having…
To place in a museum.
To visit museums.

museum.ety: From Latin mūsēum (“library, study”), from Ancient Greek Μουσεῖον (Mouseîon), shrine of the Muses (Μοῦσα (Moûsa)). Doublet of mosaic.

ex.en: When was it that you visited the museum?
ex.ja: 君がその美術館を訪ねたのはいつだったのか。

ex.en: The museum is open from Monday to Friday.
ex.ja: その博物館は月曜から金曜まで開いています。

ex.en: This road will take you to the museum.
ex.ja: この道を行けば美術館に出ます。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mouseion（ミューズ（芸術の女神）の神殿）から。music と同じ Muse。

en: A trail for the use of, or worn by, pedestrians.
A course taken.
To make a path in, or on (something), or for (someone).
To navigate through a file system directory tree (to a desired file or folder).

path.ety:
From Middle English path, peth, from Old English pæþ (“path, track”), from Proto-West Germanic *paþ, from Proto-Germanic *paþaz (“path”). The Proto-Germanic term is possibly borrowed from Iranian, from Proto-Iranian *pántaHs, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pántaHs, from Proto-Indo-European *póntoh₁s, from the root *pent- (“to pass”), but this is disputed.
Cognates
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Paad, Pad (“path”), West Frisian paad (“path”), Dutch pad (“path”), German Pfad (“path”), German Low German Padd (“path”), Luxembourgish Pad (“path”). Indo-Iranian cognates could be Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬧𐬙𐬃 (paṇtā̊, “wa

ex.en: Does this path lead to the train station?
ex.ja: この道を行けば駅に行けますか。

ex.en: This project is on a path to failure.
ex.ja: このプロジェクトは破綻に向かうだろう。

ex.en: That's not a road. It's just a path.
ex.ja: それは道路ではなくてただの小道です。

note.ja: 古英語 pæth から。「小道・進路」。

en: An oath or affirmation; a vow.
A transaction between two persons whereby the first person undertakes in the future to render some service or gift to the second person o…
To commit to (some action or outcome), or to assure (a person) of such commitment; to make an oath or vow.
To give grounds for expectation, especially of something good.

promise.ety: From Middle English promis, promisse, borrowed from Old French promesse, from Medieval Latin prōmissa, Latin prōmissum (“a promise”), feminine and neuter past participles of prōmittō (“to send forth, to say beforehand, to promise”), from pro (“forth”) + mittere (“to send”); see mission. Compare admit, commit, permit, etc. Displaced native ġehātan (“to promise”) and ġehāt (“a promise”).

ex.en: We made a promise to meet at school.
ex.ja: 我々は学校で会う約束をした。

ex.en: Something happened and he couldn't keep his promise.
ex.ja: 何かがあって彼は約束を守る事が出来なかった。

ex.en: I have promised myself to read more books.
ex.ja: もっと本を読もうと誓いました。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ mis（送る）。前もって送り出す（言葉）→「約束（する）」。

en: To suggest a plan, course of action, etc.
To ask for a person's hand in marriage.

propose.ety: From Middle English proposen, from Anglo-Norman proposer (verb), propos (noun), Middle French proposer (verb), propos (noun), from Latin prōpōnō, prōpōnere, with conjugation altered based on poser. Doublet of propound.

ex.en: He proposed to Miss Lee and she accepted.
ex.ja: 彼がリー嬢に結婚を申し込んだところ、彼女は承諾した。

ex.en: He proposed a reform in the educational system.
ex.ja: 彼は教育制度の改革を提案した。

ex.en: He proposed that we should start at once.
ex.ja: 彼は私たちがすぐ出発することを提案した。

note.ja: pro（前に）+ pos（置く）。人前に置く →「提案する・結婚を申し込む」。

en: The acquisition of title to, or property in, anything for a price; buying for money or its equivalent.
That which is obtained for a price in money or its equivalent.
To buy, obtain by payment of a price in money or its equivalent.
To pursue and obtain; to acquire by seeking; to gain, obtain, or acquire.

purchase.ety: From Middle English purchasen, from Anglo-Norman purchacer (“seek to obtain”) from pur- (from Latin pro-) + chac(i)er (“to chase, pursue”). Compare Old French porchacier (“to follow, to chase”), which has given French pourchasser (“to chase without relent”).

ex.en: We will purchase a new car next week.
ex.ja: 我が家では来週、新車を購入するつもりだ。

ex.en: The company has purchased a new computer system.
ex.ja: その会社は新しいコンピューターシステムを購入した。

ex.en: At last, they purchased freedom with blood.
ex.ja: ついに彼らは血の犠牲によって自由を獲得した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 pourchacier（追い求める）から。pur（〜のために）+ chacier（追う）。「追い求めて手に入れる」→「購入する」。chase と同じ。

en: Condensed water falling from a cloud.
Any matter moving or falling, usually through air, and especially if liquid or otherwise figuratively identifiable with raindrops.
To have rain fall from the sky.
To fall as or like rain.

ex.ja: 去年は雨が多かった。

ex.en: The weather bureau says it will rain tonight.
ex.ja: 気象庁は今晩雨が降ると言っている。

ex.en: Because of rain, I could not go out.
ex.ja: 雨のため私は外出できなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 regn から。「雨」。

en: An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
Bladed or pointed weapons, as swords, javelins, daggers.
Made of steel.
Similar to steel in color, strength, or the like; steely.
To edge, cover, or point with steel.
To electroplate an item (particularly an engraving plate) with a layer of iron.

steel.ety: From Middle English stele, stel, from Old English stīele, from Proto-West Germanic *stahlī (“something made of steel”), enlargement of *stahl (“steel”), from Proto-Germanic *stahlą, from *stah- or *stag- (“to be firm, rigid”), from Proto-Indo-European *stak- (“to stay, to be firm”). Compare Scots stele, Yola stehli, German Stahl, Dutch staal, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish stål.

ex.en: Building the steel factory was a great enterprise.
ex.ja: その製鉄工場を建てるのは非常に大変な事業だった。

ex.en: Steel production will increase 2% this month from last month.
ex.ja: 今月の鉄鋼の生産は、先月より２％増になるだろう。

ex.en: That town is the center of the steel industry.
ex.ja: その町は鉄鋼業の中心地である。

note.ja: 古英語 stēle から。stay（とどまる・しっかりしている）と同系。「硬いもの」→「鋼鉄」。

Formidable, powerful.

ex.ja: ひどい撃ち合いがおとといの晩に始まったのよ。

ex.en: Never have I heard so terrible a story.
ex.ja: そんなひどい話は聞いたことがない。

ex.en: The meat was giving off a terrible smell.
ex.ja: その肉はひどい臭いがしていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 terribilis（恐ろしい）から。terrere（恐れさせる）。terror、terrify と同じ。

en: To become sleepy or weary.
To make sleepy or weary.
US and Canada spelling of tyre: The rubber covering on a wheel.
A child's apron covering the upper part of the body, and tied with tape or cord; a pinafore. Also tier.

From Middle English tiren, tirien, teorien, from Old English tȳrian, tēorian (“to fail, cease, become weary, be tired, exhausted; tire, weary, exhaust”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from Proto-West Germanic *teuʀōn (“to cease”), which is possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dews- (“to fail, be behind, lag”). Compare Ancient Greek δεύομαι (deúomai, “to lack”), Sanskrit दोष (dóṣa, “crime, fault, vice, deficiency”).

ex.en: Now that you are tired, you'd better rest.
ex.ja: 君は疲れているので、休んだ方がよい。

ex.en: Sick and tired, she went to bed early.
ex.ja: 気分が悪く、疲れていたので、彼女は早めに就寝した。

ex.en: When I got home, I was very tired.
ex.ja: 家に着いた時、私はたいへん疲れていた。

note.ja: 「疲れる」は古英語 tēorian から。「タイヤ」は attire（装い）の短縮で、車輪に「着せる」もの。別語。

Any of various crimes related (depending on jurisdiction) to weapons, prostitution, pornography, gambling, alcohol, tobacco, or drugs.
in place of; subordinate to; designating a person below another in rank

ex.en: The Vice-President transmitted the message by radio.
ex.ja: 副大統領はメッセージをラジオで伝えた。

note.ja: 「悪徳」はラテン語 vitium（欠点）から。「副〜」（vice-president）はラテン語 vice（〜の代わりに）からで別語。

en: Of a somewhat high temperature, often but not always connoting that the high temperature is pleasant rather than uncomfortable.
Friendly and with affection.
To make or keep warm.
To become warm, to heat up.

ex.ja: そこは一年中暖かい。

ex.en: It is too warm for a fire today.
ex.ja: きょうは暖かいから火はいらない。

note.ja: 古英語 wearm から。「暖かい」→「心のこもった」。

en: Impressed with fear or apprehension; in fear.
Regretful, sorry; expressing a reluctance to face an unpleasant situation.

afraid.ety: From Middle English affrayed, affraied, past participle of afraien (“to affray”), from Anglo-Norman afrayer (“to terrify, disquiet, disturb”), from Old French effreer, esfreer (“to disturb, remove the peace from”), from es- (“out”) + freer (“to secure, secure the peace”), from Frankish *friþu (“security, peace”), from Proto-Germanic *friþuz (“peace”), from Proto-Germanic *frijōną (“to free; to love”), from Proto-Indo-European *prāy-, *prēy- (“to like, love”). ex.en: I was almost afraid to talk to you.
ex.ja: 君に話しかけるのがどうもこわかったのです。

ex.en: I'm afraid I didn't explain it too well.
ex.ja: どうも私の説明はちっともうまくなかったようだ。

ex.en: I am afraid I must be going now.
ex.ja: ではこれで失礼します。

note.ja: affray（おびえさせる）の過去分詞。古フランス語 effreer。「おびえた」。

A fermented extract of the roots and other parts of various plants, as spruce, ginger, sassafras, etc.

To drink beer.

ex.ja: 気が抜けないうちにビールを飲んで下さい。

ex.en: Would you care for another glass of beer?
ex.ja: もう一杯ビールはいかがですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 biber（飲み物）から。bibere（飲む）。

en: The line or frontier area separating political or geographical regions.
The outer edge of something.
To put a border on something.
To form a border around; to bound.

ex.en: How far are we from the Canadian border?
ex.ja: カナダとの国境までどれぐらいですか？

ex.en: Both Canada and Mexico border on the United States.
ex.ja: カナダとメキシコは両方とも合衆国と接している。

ex.en: We'll be across the border by tomorrow.
ex.ja: 明日中には国境を越えます。

note.ja: 古フランス語 bordure（縁）から。bord（船べり・縁）。「縁」→「国境」。board（船べり）と同系。

Of, belonging to, or relating to Canadian English.
A native or inhabitant of Canada.

ex.en: I fell in love with a Canadian girl.
ex.ja: カナダの女の子に恋してしまった。

note.ja: Canada + -ian。「カナダの」。

en: One of the simplest or essential parts or principles of which anything consists, or upon which the constitution or fundamental powers of …
Any one of the types of atom distinguished by having a certain number of protons in its nucleus.

element.ety:
From Middle English element, from Old French element, from Latin elementum (“a first principle, element, rudiment”) (see further etymology there).
The verb is from Middle English elementen, from the noun.

ex.en: Hard work is the main element of success.
ex.ja: 勤勉は成功のための重要な要素だ。

ex.en: I am out of my element in math.
ex.ja: 私は数学は苦手だ。

ex.en: Hard work is an essential element of success.
ex.ja: 努力は成功の基本要素である。

note.ja: ラテン語 elementum（基本要素）から。「要素・元素」→ 自然の力（the elements：風雨）。elementary と同じ。

en: Someone who is hostile to, feels hatred towards, opposes the interests of, or intends injury to someone else.
A hostile force or nation; a fighting member of such a force or nation.
To make an enemy of.

enemy.ety: From Middle English enemy, enemye, enmy, borrowed from Old French enemi, anemi (Modern French ennemi), from Latin inimīcus, from in- (“not”) + amīcus (“friend”). Displaced Middle English fend (“enemy”), from Old English fēond (“enemy”), which survived into Modern English as fiend, but with a different meaning. Doublet of inimic.

ex.en: Our army attacked the enemy during the night.
ex.ja: わが軍は敵に夜襲をかけた。

ex.en: The army abandoned the town to the enemy.
ex.ja: 軍はその町から兵を引いて敵に明け渡した。

ex.en: An enemy yesterday can be a friend today.
ex.ja: 昨日の敵が今日の友になることもある。

note.ja: ラテン語 inimicus ＝ in（否定）+ amicus（友）。「友でない者」→「敵」。amicable と同じ。

en: To make sure or certain of something (usually some future event or condition).

ensure.ety: From Middle English ensuren, from Anglo-Norman enseurer, from Old French seur (“sure”). Doublet of insure.

ex.en: I can ensure a job for you.
ex.ja: 私はあなたに仕事を確保できる。

ex.en: I can't ensure that she will be here tomorrow.
ex.ja: 彼女が明日ここに来るかどうか請け合えない。

ex.en: I can't ensure that he will pass the examination.
ex.ja: 彼が試験に通るかどうか保証できない。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ sure（確かな）。「確実にする」。insure、assure と同系。

To enter (something), making it full.
A sufficient or more than sufficient amount.
An amount that fills a container.

fill.ety:
From Middle English fillen, fullen, from Old English fyllan (“to fill, fill up, replenish, satisfy; complete, fulfill”), from Proto-West Germanic *fullijan, from Proto-Germanic *fullijaną (“to make full, fill”), from *fullaz (“full”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós (“full”).
Cognate with Scots fill (“to fill”), West Frisian folje (“to fill”), Low German füllen (“to fill”), Dutch vullen (“to fill”), German füllen (“to fill”), Danish fylde (“to fill”), Swedish fylla (“to fill”), Norwegian fylle (“to fill”), Icelandic fylla (“to fill”) and Latin plenus (“full”)

ex.en: I'll find someone to fill in for you.
ex.ja: 君の代行者を見つけよう。

ex.en: We've got to fill this hole with something.
ex.ja: この穴を何かで詰めなくては。

ex.en: I filled in my name on the paper.
ex.ja: 紙に自分の名を記入した。

note.ja: 古英語 fyllan から。full（いっぱいの）と同じ語根。「満たす」。

en: A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.
Any dense collection or amount.
To cover an area with trees.

forest.ety:
Inherited from Middle English forest, from Old French forest, from Early Medieval Latin forestis. The Latin could be:
* from foris (“outside”), as in forestis (silva) "(wood) outside,"
* or from Frankish or Proto-West Germanic *furhisti (“forest, fir-grove, wooded land”), equivalent to fir + hurst. In which case, related to Old English fyrhþe (“forested land”), Old High German forst, forsti (“forest”), Old Norse fýri (“pine forest”). Doublet of frith.
Cognate with Dutch vorst (“copse, grove, woodland”), German Forst (“forest”).
In this sense, mostly displaced the native Middle English wode, fr

ex.en: The boy lost his way in the forest.
ex.ja: その少年は森の中で道に迷った。

ex.en: A forest fire broke out in this area.
ex.ja: この地域で山火事が起こった。

ex.en: You can see many animals in this forest.
ex.ja: この森では多くの動物が見られる。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 forestis（外の森）から。foris（外に）。囲いの外の森 →「森林」。foreign と同じ。

ex.ja: 2週間ぐらいそこに滞在するつもりだったんです。

ex.en: I'd intended to visit the temple last week.
ex.ja: 先週そのお寺を訪問するつもりだったんです。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ tend（伸ばす）。心を〜の方へ伸ばす →「意図する・〜するつもりである」。intention（意図）。

ex.ja: 月が雲の後ろから現れた。

ex.en: The moon is coming up over the mountains.
ex.ja: 月が山の向こうから上がりつつある。

ex.en: Nor are there any woods on the moon.
ex.ja: 月には森も無い。

The continuous body of salt water covering a majority of the Earth's surface.

ex.en: I'd like a room facing the ocean instead.

ex.en: Our plane was flying over the Pacific Ocean.
ex.ja: われわれの飛行機は太平洋の上を飛んで行った。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 Ōkeanos（世界を取り巻く大河の神）から。「大洋」。

en: Total income or cash flow minus expenditures. The money or other benefit a non-governmental organization or individual receives in exchan…
To benefit (somebody), be of use to (somebody).
To benefit, gain.

profit.ety: From Middle English profit, from Old French profit (Modern French profit), from Latin prōfectus (“advance, progress, growth, increase, profit”), from proficiō (“to go forward, advance, make progress, be profitable or useful”). Doublet of profect.

ex.en: A third party makes off with the profits.
ex.ja: 漁夫の利を占める。

ex.en: It was to his profit to do so.
ex.ja: そうするのが彼のためだった。

ex.en: Mr Jones believes in hard work and profits.
ex.ja: ジョーンズ氏は一生懸命働いて利益を得ることを良いことだと信じている。

en: An effort, process, or operation designed to establish or discover a fact or truth; an act of testing; a test; a trial.
The degree of evidence which convinces the mind of any truth or fact, and produces belief; a test by facts or arguments which induce, or …
Used in proving or testing.
Firm or successful in resisting.
To proofread.
To make resistant, especially to water.

proof.ety: From Middle English proof, from Old French prove, from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from Latin probō (“to prove”); see prove; compare also the doublet probe.

ex.en: It's so obvious we don't need proof.
ex.ja: 明白すぎて証明を要しない。

ex.en: We've got no proof Tom did this.
ex.ja: トムがやったという証拠は何もない。

ex.en: You don't have any proof, do you?
ex.ja: 証拠もないんだろ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 prueve から。ラテン語 probare（証明する）。prove と同じ。waterproof は「水の試練に耐える」。

en: A member of a ground-based army, of any rank, but especially an enlisted member.
An enlisted member of a military service, as distinguished from a commissioned officer.
To continue steadfast; to keep striving.
To serve as a soldier.

soldier.ety:
Inherited from Middle English soudeour, from Old French soudier or soudeour (“mercenary”), from Medieval Latin soldarius (“soldier (one having pay)”), from Late Latin solidus, a type of coin. Displaced Old English cempa (whence obsolete kemp).
(red herring): An allusion to soldiers' red uniforms; red herring is, reciprocally, a slang term for "soldier".

ex.en: Many soldiers were killed in World War II.
ex.ja: 多くの兵士が第二次世界大戦で亡くなった。

ex.en: The soldiers' mission was to destroy the bridge.
ex.ja: 兵士たちの使命はその橋を破壊することだった。

ex.en: The soldiers were making for the enemy camp.
ex.ja: 兵士たちは敵の陣地へ向かって進んでいた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 soudier から。sou（貨幣）、ラテン語 solidus（金貨）。「給料で雇われた兵」。

A garment or set of garments suitable and/or required for a given task or activity: space suit, boiler suit, protective suit, swimsuit.
To make proper or suitable; to adapt or fit.
To be suitable or apt for one's image.

attorney.ety: From Middle English attourne, from Old French atorné, past participle of atorner, atourner, aturner (“to attorn”), in the sense of "one appointed or constituted".

ex.ja: 弁護士は彼女が潔白だという有力な証拠を握っている。

ex.en: The district attorney wasn't content with a two-year sentence.
ex.ja: 懲役２年の判決に地方検事は不満だった。

ex.en: Could you find me an attorney?
ex.ja: 弁護士をお世話願えませんか。

en: An action, state of mind, or object one has an obligation to perform for another, adopt toward another, or give to another.

ex.en: Our debt is more than we can pay.
ex.ja: 我々の借金は我々の返済能力を超えている。

ex.ja: われわれは彼の借金の支払いを請求した。

ex.ja: こんなに借金を私がどうして払えようか。

en: Of or relating to the home.
Of or relating to activities normally associated with the home, wherever they actually occur.
A maid or household servant.
A domestic dispute, whether verbal or violent.

domestic.ety: From Middle French domestique, from Latin domesticus, from domus (“house, home”).

ex.ja: 家庭用品は三階にあります。

ex.en: She is said to be a domestic woman.
ex.ja: 彼女は家庭的な女性だそうです。

ex.en: We consumers must buy more domestic products.
ex.ja: 我々消費者は国産品をもっと買わなければならない。

ex.ja: 君がはいている靴は、かなり高い値段がするように見える。

ex.ja: もっと値段が高い時計を買いたい。

ex.en: It is too expensive for me to buy.
ex.ja: それは高価すぎて私には買えない。

The act of jumping; a leap; a spring; a bound.

jump.ety:

note.ja: 16世紀からの語。擬音的な語とされる。「跳ぶ」。

The act or fact of launching (a ship/vessel, a project, a new book, etc.).

ex.ja: 息子を世間に出した。

ex.ja: 敵は我々に攻撃を開始した。

ex.ja: 彼は自分の事業を始めようとしている。

ex.ja: この詩は本来フランス語で書かれていた。

ex.ja: 彼らはもともと農業をやっていました。

Inherited from Middle English factour, from Middle French facteur, Anglo-Norman factour, and their etymon Latin factor (“a doer, maker, performer”), from factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”).

ex.en: These two factors are independent of each other.
ex.ja: これら二つの要因は互いに無関係である。

ex.en: Great effort was one factor in his success.
ex.ja: 大変な努力が彼の成功の一因であった。

ex.en: Several factors operated to help prices go up.
ex.ja: 物価を押し上げるのにいくつかの要因が作用した。

note.ja: fac（する・作る）+ or。何かを作り出すもの →「要因・要素」。

en: To give (someone or something) food to eat.
To eat (usually of animals).
Food given to (especially herbivorous) non-human animals.
Something supplied continuously.

feed.ety: From Middle English feden, from Old English fēdan (“to feed”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdijan, from Proto-Germanic *fōdijaną (“to feed”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to guard, graze, feed”). Cognate with West Frisian fiede (“to nourish, feed”), Dutch voeden (“to feed”), Danish føde (“to bring forth, feed”), Swedish föda (“to bring forth, feed”), Icelandic fæða (“to feed”), and more distantly with Latin pāscō (“feed, nourish”, verb) through Indo-European. More at food, fodder.

ex.en: The data has been fed into the computer.
ex.ja: そのデータはコンピューターに入力された。

ex.en: I am fed up with this wet weather.
ex.ja: この雨模様の天気はうんざりだ。

ex.en: We feed our dog three times a day.
ex.ja: 私たちは１日につき３回犬に食事を与える。

note.ja: 古英語 fēdan から。food（食べ物）と同じ語根。「食べ物を与える」→ 情報を「供給する」。

en: Made of, or relating to, gold.
Having a color or other richness suggestive of gold.
brassy drummer, brassy chub, etc. (Kyphosus vaigiensis), a fish found in southeast Asia.
To become gold or golden (in color).
To make golden or like gold.

golden.ety:
From Middle English golden, a restored form (due to the noun gold) of earlier Middle English gulden, gylden, gilden ("golden"; > English gilden), from Old English gylden (“golden”), from Proto-West Germanic *gulþīn, from Proto-Germanic *gulþīnaz (“golden, made of gold”), equivalent to gold + -en.
Cognate with Dutch gouden, gulden (“golden”), German gülden, golden (“golden”), Danish gylden (“golden”). Doublet of gilden. More at gold.

ex.en: The Golden Gate Bridge is made of iron.
ex.ja: 金門橋は鉄でできている。

ex.en: How long is the Golden Gate Bridge?
ex.ja: 金門橋はどれくらいの長さですか。

ex.en: She was a girl with golden hair.
ex.ja: 彼女は金髪の少女だった。

note.ja: gold（金）+ -en（〜の）。「金の」→「絶好の」（golden opportunity）。wooden と同じ作り。

en: To give (permission or wish).
To give (bestow upon or confer, particularly in answer to prayer or request).
The act of granting or giving
The yielding or admission of something in dispute.

grant.ety: From Middle English granten, graunten, grantien, grauntien, from Anglo-Norman granter, graunter, from Old French granter, graunter, graanter, greanter (“to promise, assure, guarantee, confirm, ratify”), from a merger of Old French garantir, guarantir (“to guarantee, assure, vouch for”) (see English guarantee) and earlier cranter, craanter, creanter (“to allow, permit”), from an assumed Medieval Latin *credentāre, from Latin credere (“to believe, trust”). Alternatively, a regular reflex of Medieval Latin *credentāre with regular voicing of /k/ before a liquid plus low vowel. More at guarantee,

ex.en: We take it for granted that television exists.
ex.ja: テレビの存在を当然のことと思っている。

ex.en: He was granted permission to go home early.
ex.ja: 彼は早く帰ってもいい許可を得た。

ex.en: I took it for granted that you'd come.
ex.ja: 私は君が来るのを当然だと思っていた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 granter（保証する）から。ラテン語 credere（信じる）。「保証して与える」→「助成金」。credit と同系。

en: A professional person with a graduate law degree that qualifies for legal work (such as Juris Doctor)
A professional person qualified (as by a law degree or bar exam) and authorized to practice law as an attorney-at-law, solicitor, advocat…
To practice law.
To perform, or attempt to perform, the work of a lawyer.

lawyer.ety: From Middle English lawiere, lawier, lawer, equivalent to law + -yer.

ex.en: Jim is not a lawyer but a doctor.
ex.ja: ジムは弁護士でなく医者だ。

ex.en: I have the right to call my lawyer.
ex.ja: 私には、弁護士に電話をする権利がありますよ。

ex.en: I have a cousin who is a lawyer.
ex.ja: 私には弁護士のいとこがいる。

note.ja: law（法律）+ -yer。「法律家」→「弁護士」。sawyer（木びき）と同じ作り。

en: A limb or appendage that an animal uses for support or locomotion on land.
In humans, the lower limb extending from the groin to the ankle.
To remove the legs from an animal carcass.
To build legs onto a platform or stage for support.

leg.ety:
From Middle English leg, legge, from Old Norse leggr (“leg, calf, bone of the arm or leg, hollow tube, stalk”), from Proto-Germanic *lagjaz, *lagwijaz (“leg, thigh”) (see it for more).
Cognate with Scots leg (“leg”), Icelandic leggur (“leg, limb”), Norwegian Bokmål legg (“leg”), Norwegian Nynorsk legg (“leg”), Swedish lägg (“leg, shank, shaft”), Danish læg (“leg”), Lombardic lagi (“thigh, shank, leg”), Latin lacertus (“limb, arm”), Persian لنگ (leng). Upon borrowing, mostly displaced the native Old English term sċanca (Modern English shank).

ex.en: I can't walk because of my broken leg.
ex.ja: わたしは足の骨折のために歩けない。

ex.en: A ball hit her on the right leg.
ex.ja: ボールが彼女の右足に当たった。

ex.en: Kick with your legs straight to go forward.
ex.ja: ばた足をして進もう。

note.ja: 古北欧語 leggr から。「脚」→ 旅の「一区間」。

en: A limit that cannot be exceeded; a bound. (Now chiefly in set phrases.)
An (unspecified) portion or quantity.
To ascertain the quantity of a unit of material via calculated comparison with respect to a standard.
To be of (a certain size), to have (a certain measurement).

ex.en: No woman could measure up to his standard.
ex.ja: 彼のめがねにかなう女性はいなかった。

ex.en: In the town there was a measure of peace.
ex.ja: 市街にはいくぶん平和があった。

ex.en: We took strong measures to prevent it.
ex.ja: 私たちはそれを防止する強硬な対策を講じた。

en: To understand wrongly, taking one thing or person for another.
An error.
A pitch which was intended to be pitched in a hard-to-hit location, but instead ends up in an easy-to-hit place.

mistake.ety:
From Middle English mistaken, from Old Norse mistaka (“to take in error, to miscarry”); equivalent to mis- + take. Cognate with Icelandic mistaka (“to mistake”), Swedish missta (“to mistake”) (before apocope misstaga).
The noun, which replaced earlier mistaking, is derived from the verb. Compare Swedish misstag (“mistake”, noun), Faroese mistak (“mitake”, noun), Icelandic mistak (“mistake”, noun).

ex.en: You made the same mistake as last time.
ex.ja: 君は前と同じ誤りを犯した。

ex.en: You have made the very same mistake again.
ex.ja: 君はまったく同じ間違いをまたやったね。

ex.en: You made the mistake on purpose, didn't you?
ex.ja: 君は、故意に間違いを犯したんだね。

note.ja: mis（誤って）+ take（取る）。北欧語 mistaka。「取り違える」→「間違い」。

en: An adherent of Islam.
A person who internalizes the Islamic cultural tradition, or way of thinking, as a frame of reference.
Being or relating to a believer of Islam.

Muslim.ety: Borrowed around 1615 from Arabic مُسْلِم (muslim, “one who submits”), the active participle of أَسْلَمَ (ʔaslama, “he submitted”), verb form IV from the triliteral root س ل م (s l m), "to be whole, intact". The verbal noun إسْلام (ʔislām) means literally "submission". In a religious sense, الْإِسْلَام (al-ʔislām) translates to "faith, piety", and مُسْلِم (muslim) to "one who has (religious) faith or piety".

ex.en: I was born in a Muslim-majority country.
ex.ja: 私はイスラム教徒の多い国で生まれました。

ex.en: There are a lot of Muslims in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本にはたくさんムスリムの方がいます。

ex.en: He was born and raised as a Muslim.
ex.ja: 彼は、ムスリムとして生まれ育った。

note.ja: アラビア語 muslim（神に身をゆだねた者）から。Islam（服従）と同じ語根 s-l-m。salaam（平和）とも同じ。

en: A raised stage from which speeches are made and on which musical and other performances are made.
A raised floor for any purpose, e.g. for workmen during construction, or formerly for military cannon.
To furnish with or shape into a platform
To place on, or as if on, a platform.

platform.ety: From Middle French plateforme (“a flat form”), from plate (“flat”) (from Old French plat, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “flat”)) + forme (“form”) (from Latin fōrma (“shape; figure; form”)); compare flatscape.

ex.en: Which is the platform for the London train?
ex.ja: ロンドン行きの列車のプラットホームはどちらですか。

ex.en: John is waiting for Mary on the platform.
ex.ja: ジョンはプラットホームでメアリーを待っている。

ex.en: She came close to falling off the platform.
ex.ja: 彼女はもう少しでホームから落ちそうだった。

note.ja: フランス語 plate-forme（平らな形）から。「台」→「（駅の）ホーム」→「基盤」。plate、form と同じ。

en: A small and rather deep area of (usually) fresh water, as one supplied by a spring, or occurring in the course of a stream or river; a re…
Any small body of standing or stagnant water; a puddle.
To form a pool.

pool.ety:
From Middle English pool, pole, pol, from Old English pōl (“pool”), from Proto-West Germanic pōl, from Proto-Germanic *pōlaz (“pool, pond”), from Proto-Indo-European *bōlos (“bog, marsh”).
Cognate with Scots puil (“pool”), Saterland Frisian Pol (“pool”), West Frisian poel (“pool”), Dutch poel (“pool”), German Low German Pohl, Pool, Pul (“pool”), German Pfuhl (“quagmire, mudhole”), Danish pøl (“puddle”), Swedish pöl (“puddle, pool”), Icelandic pollur (“puddle”), Lithuanian bala (“puddle”), Latvian bala (“a muddly, treeless depression”), Russian боло́то (bolóto, “swamp, bog, marsh”).

ex.en: The swimming pool is open to the public.
ex.ja: この水泳プールは一般に公開されている。

ex.en: I've got a pass for the swimming pool.
ex.ja: 私はそこのプールのパスを持っている。

ex.en: I go to the city pool every day.
ex.ja: 毎日市営プールに行きます。

note.ja: 「水たまり・プール」は古英語 pōl から。「共同出資する」はフランス語 poule（めんどり・賭け金）からで別語。

en: A steady look, a gaze.
One's concern for another; esteem; relation, reference.
To look at; to observe.
To consider, look upon (something) in a given way etc.

regard.ety: From Middle English regard, regarde, reguard, from Anglo-Norman reguard, from regarder, reguarder. Attested in Middle English starting around the mid 14th century. Piecewise doublet of reward; compare also guard, ward, guardian, and so on.

ex.en: The bank director was held in high regard.
ex.ja: その頭取は尊敬を集めていた。

ex.en: What's your opinion with regard to this matter?
ex.ja: この問題に関してどのようにお考えですか。

ex.en: I have nothing to say in this regard.
ex.ja: この点については何も言うことはありません。

note.ja: 古フランス語 regarder（見る）から。re + garder（見守る）。「見なす・敬意」。guard と同じ。

en: The manner in which two things may be associated.
A member of one's extended family; a relative.

relation.ety: From Middle English relacion, relacioun, from Anglo-Norman relacioun and Old French relacion (whence French relation), from Latin relātiō, noun of process form from perfect passive participle relātus (“related”), from verb referō (“to refer, to relate”), from prefix re- (“again”) + ferō (“to bear, to carry”). By surface analysis, relate + -ion. Doublet of relazione.

ex.en: We have no business relations with the firm.
ex.ja: 当店はその会社と取引関係はありません。

ex.en: Relations with Canada remained correct and cool.
ex.ja: カナダとの関係は適切かつ冷静な状態が保たれていた。

ex.en: You are interested in a career in foreign relations.
ex.ja: 国際関係の仕事に興味があるのですね。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ lat（運ばれた）+ ion。元へ運び戻して結びつけること →「関係・親族」。relate（関係づける）。

en: A course or way which is traveled or passed.
A regular itinerary of stops, or the path followed between these stops, such as for delivery or passenger transportation.
To direct or divert along a particular course.
To send (information) through a router.

route.ety: From Middle English route, from Old French route, from Latin rupta [via] (literally “a path made by force”). Compare Modern French route. See routine. Further via Latin ruptus related with bankrupt. Unrelated to road.

ex.en: The party, therefore, had to take another route.
ex.ja: 一行は、そのため、別のルートを取らねばならなかった。

ex.en: I must have lost the key en route.
ex.ja: 道の途中で鍵を落としたに違いない。

ex.en: May I have a bus route map?
ex.ja: 路線地図をもらえますか。

note.ja: 古フランス語 route（道）から。ラテン語 via rupta（切り開かれた道）。rupture と同じ rupt。routine（決まった道筋）。

en: A procedural plan, usually but not necessarily tabular in nature, indicating a sequence of operations and the planned times at which thos…
A serial record of items, systematically arranged.
To create a time-schedule.
To plan (an activity or event) for a specific date or time.

schedule.ety:
Inherited from Middle English cedule, from Middle French cedule (whence French cédule), from Old French cedule, from Late Latin schedula (“papyrus strip”), diminutive of Latin scheda, from Ancient Greek σχέδη (skhédē, “papyrus leaf”), from Proto-Hellenic *skʰíd͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *skid-yé-ti, from *skeyd- (“to divide, split”). Doublet of cedula and cedule.
This word was historically pronounced /ˈsɛdjuːl/, /ˈsɛdʒuːl/; the pronunciations with /ʃ/ and /sk/ are due to the spelling (the latter may have been reinforced by learned influence); compare schism.

ex.en: You should carry out the plan on schedule.
ex.ja: 君はその計画を予定通り実行すべきだ。

ex.en: We cannot make a change in our schedule.
ex.ja: 私達の予定は変更できません。

ex.en: At any rate, we can't change the schedule.
ex.ja: いずれにしてもスケジュールは変更できない。

note.ja: ラテン語 schedula（小さな紙片）から。ギリシャ語 skhedē（パピルスの切れ端）。「一覧表」→「予定表」。

Derived from or consistent with the scientific method.

en: A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer u…
A piece of metal designed to be attached to a horse's foot as a means of protection; a horseshoe.
To put shoes on one's own feet.
To put shoes on someone or something else's feet, especially to put horseshoes on a horse.

ex.en: Your shoes do not go with the suit.
ex.ja: 君の靴はその服と合わない。

ex.en: The shoes you are wearing look rather expensive.
ex.ja: 君がはいている靴は、かなり高い値段がするように見える。

ex.en: Before buying shoes, you should try them on.
ex.ja: 靴を買う前には、試しに履いてみなければならない。

note.ja: 古英語 scōh から。「靴」。horseshoe（蹄鉄）。

en: The visible vapor/vapour, gases, and fine particles given off by burning or smoldering material.
A cigarette.
To inhale and exhale the smoke from a burning cigarette or cigar, burning material in a pipe, etc.
To inhale and exhale tobacco smoke.

smoke.ety: From Middle English smoke, from Old English smoca (“smoke”), probably a derivative of the verb (see below). Related to Dutch smook (“smoke”), Middle Low German smôk (“smoke”), German Schmauch (“smoke (from a gun barrel)”).

ex.en: You should make an effort to stop smoking.
ex.ja: 君は禁煙するよう努力すべきだ。

ex.en: You had better not smoke while on duty.
ex.ja: 勤務中はタバコを吸わない方がいいよ。

ex.en: It is necessary for you to stop smoking.
ex.ja: 君は煙草を吸うのをやめることが必要だ。

note.ja: 古英語 smoca から。「煙」→「たばこを吸う」。

en: A group of people organized for some common purpose, usually of about ten members.
A unit of tactical military personnel, or of police officers, usually of about ten members.
To act as part of, or on behalf of, a squad.
To transport by ambulance.

ex.en: My brother is a member of the rescue squad.
ex.ja: 兄はレスキュー隊のメンバーだ。

en: Improper treatment or usage; application to a wrong or bad purpose; an unjust, corrupt or wrongful practice or custom.
Misuse; improper use; perversion.
To put to a wrong use; to misapply; to use improperly; to use for a wrong purpose or end; to pervert
To injure; to maltreat; to hurt; to treat with cruelty, especially repeatedly.

abuse.ety: From Middle English abusen, then from either Old French abus (“improper use”), or from Latin abūsus (“misused, using up”), perfect active participle of abūtor (“make improper use of, consume, abuse”), from ab (“away”) + ūtor (“to use”). Equivalent to ab- + use.

ex.en: Tom has a history of drug abuse.
ex.ja: トムは薬物乱用の経験がある。

ex.en: He flung a stream of abuse at me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に悪態を浴びせかけた。

ex.en: They burst out into a storm of abuse.
ex.ja: 彼らは激しくののしり始めた。

note.ja: ab（離れて）+ uti（使う）。「正しい使い方から外れる」→「乱用・虐待」。use と同じ。

en: Displaying or feeling anger.
Inflamed and painful.

ex.ja: トムはその高校生達に腹を立てた。

ex.ja: どうして彼はそんなことを怒っているのですか。

ex.en: What made him so angry then, I wonder?
ex.ja: どうして彼はあの時あんなに怒ったのだろう。

note.ja: anger（怒り）+ -y。anger は北欧語 angr（苦悩）、anxious、anguish と同系。

en: A person who seeks to be elected or appointed to a position or privilege.
A person who is thought likely or worthy to gain a position or privilege.
To stand as a candidate for an office, typically for a religious one.

candidate.ety: From Latin candidātus (“a person who is standing for public office”, noun), from candidus (“dazzling white, shining, clear”) + -ātus, -āta, -ātum (participial adjective-forming suffix), in reference to Roman candidates wearing bleached white togas as a symbol of purity at a public forum. ex.en: He is one of the American presidential candidates.
ex.ja: 彼はアメリカ大統領候補者の一人である。

ex.en: He came forward as a candidate for Congress.
ex.ja: 彼は議員に自分から進んで立候補した。

ex.en: Many Republicans didn't vote for their own candidate.
ex.ja: 多くの共和党員が自党の候補者には投票しなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 candidatus（白い服を着た人）から。candidus（白い）。古代ローマの立候補者は白いトガを着た。candle と同じ。

en: Providing physical comfort and ease; agreeable.
In a state of comfort and content.
A stuffed or quilted coverlet for a bed; a comforter.

comfortable.ety: From Middle English comfortable, from Old French confortable, from conforter. By surface analysis, comfort + -able.

ex.en: This house is very comfortable to live in.
ex.ja: この家は住むのにとても快適だ。

ex.en: Here's a comfortable chair you can sit in.
ex.ja: あなたが座れる快適な椅子がここにあります。

ex.ja: 眼がわるい人は遠くが見えない。

ex.en: Everyone has their own strong and weak points.
ex.ja: 誰にでも得手不得手がある。

note.ja: 古北欧語 veikr（しなやかな）から。「弱い」。

en: Someone or something that takes part in some action; a doer, an agent.
A person who acts a part in a theatrical play or (later) in film or television; a dramatic performer.

actor.ety:
Etymology tree

Inherited from Middle English actour, from Anglo-Norman actor, Middle French actor, and their source, Latin āctor (“doer”), from agō (“to do”). Equivalent to act + -or. Cognate with Ancient Greek ἄκτωρ (áktōr, “leader”), from ἄγω (ágō, “lead, carry, convey, bring”).

ex.en: The actor is two years senior to me.
ex.ja: その俳優は私より２歳年上だ。

ex.en: Sitting next to me was a famous actor.
ex.ja: 私の隣に有名な俳優が座った。

ex.en: To tell the truth, that actor is married.
ex.ja: 実を言うと、あの俳優は結婚しているんだ。

note.ja: act（演じる）+ -or。ラテン語 agere（行う）。「行う人」→「俳優」。

en: A complete domicile occupying only part of a building, especially one for rent; a flat.
A room within a house.

apartment.ety: From French appartement, from Italian appartamento, from Spanish apartamiento (“separation, seclusion”), equivalent to apart + -ment. See apart and -ment.

ex.en: What happened? There's water all over the apartment.
ex.ja: 何が起こったの？アパート全体水浸しだよ。

ex.en: There is an apartment house near my house.
ex.ja: 私の家の近くにアパートがあります。

ex.en: He is living in an apartment at present.
ex.ja: 彼は現在アパート暮らしをしている。

note.ja: a（〜へ）+ part（分ける）+ ment。分けられた区画 →「アパート（の一室）」。

ex.en: Many immigrants to Britain have come from Asia.
ex.ja: 英国への多くの移民はアジアからきている。

ex.en: Japan is in the eastern part of Asia.
ex.ja: 日本はアジアの東部にあります。

ex.en: Europe has a smaller population than Asia.
ex.ja: ヨーロッパはアジアより人口が少ない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 Asia から。古代アナトリア（現在のトルコ）の地名とされる。

en: A series of interconnected rings or links usually made of metal.
An accessory, adornment or insignia comprising, containing or depicting a series of links.
To fasten something with a chain.
To connect as if with a chain, due to dependence, addiction, or other feelings

chain.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *katesnā
Latin catēna
Old French chaeinebor.
Middle English cheyne
English chain
From Middle English cheyne, chaine, from Old French chaeine, chaene (“chain”), from Latin catēna (“chain”), from Proto-Indo-European *kat- (“to braid, twist; hut, shed”). Doublet of catena. Displaced native Middle English rakil and rakent (from Old English racente (“chain”)); see rackan.

ex.en: The large chain store created a new branch.
ex.ja: その大チェーンストアは新しく支店を作った。

ex.en: The dog should be on a chain.
ex.ja: その犬は鎖でつないでおくべきだ。

ex.en: George put a chain on the dog.
ex.ja: ジョージはその犬に鎖をつけた。

note.ja: ラテン語 catena（鎖）から古フランス語を経た語。「鎖」→ 店の「チェーン」。

en: One of the main sections into which a published work is divided, especially a book.
A section of a work, a collection of works, or fragments of works, often manuscripts or transcriptions, created by scholars or advocates,…
To divide into chapters.
To put into a chapter.

chapter.ety: From Middle English chapitre, from Old French chapitre, from Latin capitulum (“a chapter of a book, in Medieval Latin also a synod or council”), diminutive of caput (“a head”); see capital, capitulum, and chapiter, which are doublets of chapter.

ex.en: We will deal with this problem in Chapter Three.
ex.ja: この問題は第3章で扱います。

ex.en: We'll deal with this problem in Chapter 3.
ex.ja: この問題は第3章で扱います。

ex.en: I'm going to deal with the problem in this chapter.
ex.ja: 私は本章でその問題を取り扱うつもりです。

note.ja: ラテン語 capitulum（小さな頭）から。caput（頭）。「見出し」→「章」。capital、captain と同じ。

en: To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.
To imprison: to forcibly place in a jail.
The act of committing (e.g. a database transaction), making it a permanent change; such a change.
The submission of source code or other material to a source control repository.

commit.ety: Inherited from Middle English committen, itself borrowed from Latin committō (“to bring together, join, compare, commit (a wrong), incur, give in charge, etc.”), from com- (“together”) + mittō (“to send”). See mission.

ex.en: He was believed to have committed the crime.
ex.ja: 彼は犯行に及んだと信じられていた。

ex.en: Can it be true that she committed suicide?
ex.ja: 彼女が自殺したというのは本当か。

ex.en: He admitted that he had committed the crime.
ex.ja: 彼は罪を犯したことを認めた。

note.ja: com（共に・完全に）+ mit（送る）。（人や事に）完全に送り出す →「委ねる・（罪を）犯す・約束する」。committee（委員会）も同じ。

en: Self-assurance.
A feeling of certainty; firm trust or belief; faith.

confidence.ety:
From Middle English confidence, from Latin cōnfīdentia (possibly via Old French confidence), from cōnfīdō (“believe, confide in”) from con- (“with”) + fīdō (“trust”).
By surface analysis, confide + ence.

ex.en: I have confidence in your ability to win.
ex.ja: 私はあなたは絶対勝つことができると信じています。

ex.en: Tom doesn't seem to have any self-confidence.
ex.ja: トムは自分に全く自信がないようだ。

ex.en: Where did all that self-confidence come from?
ex.ja: その自信はどこから来るの？

note.ja: con（強意）+ fidere（信じる）+ -ence。「強く信じること」→「自信・信頼」。faith、fidelity と同じ fid。

en: A person who prepares food.
The head cook of a manor house.
To prepare food for eating, typically by heating it, combining it with other ingredients, seasoning it, preparing it for serving, etc.
To apply heat to food in the course of preparing it, particularly in a way that transforms it rather than simply making it warmer.

Cog

ex.en: She has improved her skill in cooking recently.
ex.ja: 近ごろ彼女の料理の腕が上がった。

ex.en: How do you cook this fish in France?
ex.ja: フランスではこの魚をどう料理しますか。

ex.en: Do you know how to cook rice well?
ex.ja: ご飯の上手なたき方を知っていますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 coquus（料理人）から。coquere（煮る）。kitchen と同じ語源。

en: Possessing physical features, behaviors, personality traits or other properties that are mainly attributed to infants and small or cuddly…
Lovable, charming, attractive or pleasing, especially in a youthful, dainty, quaint or fun-spirited way.

cute.ety: Aphetic form of acute, originally meaning “keenly perceptive or discerning, shrewd” (1731). Meaning transferred to “pretty, fetching” by US students (slang) c. 1834. Meaning drifted further to describe the pleasing attraction to features usually possessed by the young.

ex.en: What a cute baby! May I hold her?
ex.ja: まぁかわいい赤ちゃん私にも抱かせてくれますか。

ex.en: His little sister is very cute, isn't she?
ex.ja: 彼の妹はとてもかわいいね。

ex.en: I think my girlfriend is kind of cute.
ex.ja: 僕のガールフレンドは結構かわいいと思う。

note.ja: acute（鋭い・利口な）の短縮。「抜け目のない」→（米）「かわいい」。

en: The same in one or more respects.
The same in value (status, merit, etc): having or deserving the same rights or treatment.
To be equal to, to have the same value as; to correspond to.
To make equivalent to; to cause to match.
A person or thing of equal status to others.

equal.ety:

Old Latin aiquos

Latin -ālis

Middle English equal
English equal
From Middle English equal, from Latin aequālis. Doublet of aequalis and egal.

ex.en: It is believed that all men are equal.
ex.ja: すべての人間は平等であると信じられている。

ex.en: A dollar is equal to a hundred cents.
ex.ja: １ドルは１００セントに等しい。

ex.en: I don't feel equal to doing the work.
ex.ja: 私にはその仕事はできそうにない。

note.ja: ラテン語 aequus（等しい）から。equ（等しい）+ al。→「等しい・平等な」。equator（地球を等しく分ける線→赤道）、equivalent（等しい価値の）も同じ。

en: Not real; false, fraudulent.
Insincere
Something which is not genuine, or is presented fraudulently.
A move meant to deceive an opposing player, used for gaining advantage for example when dribbling an opponent.
To make a counterfeit, to counterfeit, to forge, to falsify.
To make a false display of, to affect, to feign, to simulate.

fake.ety:
The origin is not known with certainty, although first attested in 1775 C.E. in British criminals' slang. It is probably from feak, feague (“to give a better appearance through artificial means, spruce up, embellish”), itself from German Low German fegen, from Middle Low German vēgen, from Old Saxon fegōn, from Proto-West Germanic *fegōn (“to clean up, polish”).
Akin to Dutch veeg (“a swipe”), Dutch vegen (“to sweep, wipe”); German fegen (“to sweep, to polish”). Compare also Old English fācn (“deceit, fraud”). Perhaps related also to Old Norse fjúka (“to fade, vanquish, disappear”), Old Norse

ex.en: He can't tell the real thing from the fake.
ex.ja: 彼は本物と偽物を区別できない。

ex.en: Is this diamond real or fake?
ex.ja: このダイヤモンドって、本物なのかな？偽物なのかな？

ex.en: I don't need fake friends.
ex.ja: 偽りの友達なんて要らない。

note.ja: 18世紀の泥棒の隠語から。語源ははっきりしない。「偽の」。

en: The management of money and other assets.
The science of management of money and other assets.
To conduct, or procure money for, financial operations; manage finances.
To manage financially; be financier for; provide or obtain funding for a transaction or undertaking.

finance.ety:
From Middle English finaunce, fynaunce, from Anglo-Norman, Middle French finance, from finer (“to pay ransom”) (whence also English fine (“to pay a penalty”)), from fin (“end”), from Latin fīnis.
Original English sense that appeared c. 1400 was “ending”. The sense of “ending or satisfying a debt” originated from French influence: in the sense of “ransom” appeared in the mid 15th century, in the sense of “taxation” appeared in the late 15th century. In the sense of “manage money” first recorded c. 1770.

ex.en: He claimed to be an expert in finance.
ex.ja: 彼は財政の専門家であると自称した。

ex.en: Those officials don't understand finance at all.
ex.ja: あの役人たちは全然、財政のことはわかっていない。

ex.en: More students are interested in finance than in industry.
ex.ja: 工業よりも金融に関心のある学生のほうが多い。

note.ja: ラテン語 finis（終わり）から。支払いを済ませて決着をつけること →「財政・資金」。

en: Sameness, identicalness; the quality or fact of (several specified things) being the same.
The difference or character that marks off an individual or collective from the rest of the same kind; selfhood; the sense of who somethi…

identity.ety: From Middle English ydemptite, from Middle French identité and its etymon Late Latin idemptitās, identitās, from idem (“the same”) + -tās (suffix forming abstract nouns) as a calque of Ancient Greek ταὐτότης (tautótēs, “sameness”).

ex.en: The mayor provided me with an identity card.
ex.ja: 市長は私に身分証明書をくれた。

ex.en: A student should not lose sight of his own identity.
ex.ja: 学生は自分の主体性を見失ってはならない。

ex.en: The police could not establish the identity of the man.
ex.ja: 警察はその男の身元を突きとめる事ができなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 identitas（同一性）から。idem（同じ）。「自分が自分であること」→「身元・アイデンティティ」。identify と同じ。

en: A set amount of travelling, seen as a single unit; a discrete trip, a voyage.
Any process or progression likened to a journey, especially one that involves difficulties or personal development.
To travel, to make a trip or voyage.

journey.ety: From Middle English journe, from Old French jornee, from Vulgar Latin *diurnāta, from Late Latin diurnum, from Latin diurnus, from diēs (“day”). Displaced native Old English fær and Old English faru.

ex.en: I can't afford the time for a journey.
ex.ja: 私には旅行する暇がありません。

ex.en: We are going on a journey next month.
ex.ja: 私達は来月旅行にいくつもりです。

ex.en: The twelve-hour journey had tired me out.
ex.ja: 十二時間の旅行は私をへとへとにした。

note.ja: 古フランス語 journee（一日の行程）から。ラテン語 diurnum、dies（日）。journal と同じ。

en: A room or area for preparing food.
Cuisine; style of cooking.
To do kitchen work; to prepare food.
To embellish a basic food; to season, add condiments, etc.

kitchen.ety:
From Middle English kichene, kichen, from Old English cyċen, cyċene, from Proto-West Germanic *kukinā, a borrowing from Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna (“kitchen; cuisine”), from coquō (“to cook”), from Proto-Indo-European *pekʷ- (“to cook, become ripe”).
In other languages, the cognate term often refers both to the room and the type of cooking. In English, the distinction is generally made via the etymological twins kitchen (“room”) (Latin via Germanic) and cuisine (“type of cooking”) (Latin via French).

ex.en: There is a kitchen garden behind my house.
ex.ja: 我が家の裏には家庭菜園があります。

ex.en: Don't bring that dirty dog through the kitchen.
ex.ja: その汚い犬を台所に入れないで。

ex.en: The kitchen of this house is very large.
ex.ja: この家の台所は大変広い。

note.ja: ラテン語 coquina（料理場）から。coquere（煮る）。cook と同じ語源。

en: To keep up; to preserve; to uphold (a state, condition etc.).
To declare or affirm (a clause) to be true; to assert.

maintain.ety: From Middle English mayntenen, from Old French maintenir, from Late Latin manūteneō, manūtenēre (“I support”), from Latin manū (“with/in/by the hand”, ablative of manus) + tenēre (“to hold”).

ex.en: I became unable to maintain my self-control.
ex.ja: 自制できなくなっていた。

ex.en: We build and maintain relationships with others.
ex.ja: 我々は他人との関係を構築し、維持していく。

ex.en: We should make every effort to maintain world peace.
ex.ja: 私達は世界平和の維持のためにあらゆる努力をすべきだ。

note.ja: main（= manu 手で）+ tain（保つ）。手で保つ →「維持する・主張する」。

en: An indefinite large number of.
Indefinitely large numerically; many.
Consisting of a large number of individuals or parts.

numerous.ety: From Middle English numerous from Latin numerōsus (“numerous, abundant; harmonious”), from numerus (“number”). Doublet of numerose. Analyzeable as numero- + -ous.

ex.en: Numerous stars were visible in the sky.
ex.ja: 空には多数の星が見えた。

ex.en: The store has numerous items to sell.
ex.ja: その店はたくさんの商品をそろえている。

ex.en: He has numerous friends in the Diet.
ex.ja: 彼は国会の中に大勢の友人を持っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 numerus（数）から。numer（数）+ ous（満ちた）。数に満ちた →「多数の」。number（数）も同じ。

en: With little or no sound; free of disturbing noise.
Having little motion or activity; calm.
To cause (someone or something) to become quiet.
To become quiet or calm.
The absence of sound; quietness.
The absence of movement; stillness, tranquility.
Be quiet.

quiet.ety: From Middle English quiete, from Old French quiet (adjective) and quiete (noun), from Latin quiētus, past participle of quiēscere (“to keep quiet, rest”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“rest”). Doublet of coy, quit, quite, and quietus. Largely displaced native English still in the sense of "with little or no sound".

ex.en: You must keep quiet for a few days.
ex.ja: 君は２、３日の間、静かにしていなくてはなりません。

ex.en: The boy cannot keep quiet for ten minutes.
ex.ja: その少年は１０分と静かにしていられない。

ex.en: We spent a quiet day in the country.
ex.ja: 私達は田舎で静かな一日を過ごしました。

note.ja: ラテン語 quietus（休んでいる）から。「静かな」。quit（自由にする）、quite と同じ語源。

en: The outer side of a window or door frame.
A revelation; an uncovering of what was hidden in the scene or story.
To uncover; to show and display that which was hidden or unknown.
To communicate that which could not be known or discovered without divine or supernatural instruction.

reveal.ety:
From Middle English revēlen, from Old French reveler, from Latin revēlāre (“to reveal, uncover”), from re- (“back, again”) + vēlāre (“to cover”), from vēlum (“a cloth, covering, curtain, veil, awning, sail”) (whence also English veil, English unveil, English voile, Russian вуаль (vualʹ), Russian завуали́ровать (zavualírovatʹ, “to veil”) (compare typologically)).
Also compare typologically English uncloak, dismantle, divest, invest, unmask, Russian разобла́чать (razobláčatʹ) (akin to облаче́ние (oblačénije), срыва́ть покро́вы (sryvátʹ pokróvy) (покро́в (pokróv, “cover, covering”)).

ex.en: On no account should you reveal the secret.
ex.ja: どんな事情があっても決してその秘密をもらしてはいけない。

ex.en: At last, the truth was revealed to us.
ex.ja: とうとう真実が我々に明らかにされた。

ex.en: I'm sure he will reveal his true nature.
ex.ja: きっと彼は本性を現わすよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 revelare ＝ re（取り去る）+ velum（ベール）。「ベールを取る」→「明らかにする」。veil と同じ。

For a specific purpose or reason.

ex.ja: 具体的には何すればいいの？

ex.en: Language is a specifically human characteristic.
ex.ja: 言語は人間固有の性質である。

note.ja: specific（特定の）+ -ally。ラテン語 species（種類）。「特に・具体的に」。special と同じ spec。

en: To divide fully or partly along a more or less straight line.
Of something solid, particularly wood, to break along the grain fully or partly along a more or less straight line.
Divided.
Having the middle object (group, module, etc.) equal to the direct sum of the others.
A crack or longitudinal fissure.
A breach or separation, as in a political party; a division.

split.ety:
Attested since about 1567, from Middle Dutch splitten (“to split”) and/or Middle Low German splitten (“to split”), both ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *splittjan, an intensive form of Proto-West Germanic *splītan (“to split”), from Proto-Germanic *splītaną (whence Danish splitte, Low German splieten, German spleißen), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pley- (“to split, splice”).
Compare Middle English ysplett (“split”, past participle of splatten (“to split”)), Old English speld (“splinter”), Old High German spaltan (“to split”), Middle Irish slis (“splinter”), Lithuanian spaliai (“flax sheave

ex.en: They split up after a year of marriage.
ex.ja: 結婚して一年で別れてしまった。

ex.en: I didn't want to split up with Mary.
ex.ja: メアリーとは別れたくなかった。

ex.en: I hear Tom and Mary have split up.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーが離婚したんだって。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 splitten（裂く）から。「割る・分ける」。

en: A piece of work done as part of one’s duties.
A state of diligence in work on a task.
To assign a task to; to impose a task on.
To oppress with severe or excessive burdens; to tax

task.ety: From Middle English taske (“task, tax”), from Old Northern French tasque, (compare Old French variant tasche), from Medieval Latin tasca, alteration of taxa, from Latin taxō (“to censure; to charge”). Doublet of tax.

ex.en: You may as well do the task now.
ex.ja: 君はその仕事を今した方がよい。

ex.en: It is too easy a task for him.
ex.ja: それは彼にとってはあまりにも易しすぎる仕事だ。

ex.en: The task is of great importance to them.
ex.ja: その仕事は彼らにとってとても重要だ。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 tasca（課された税）から。taxare。「割り当てられた仕事」。tax と同じ語源。

en: The cardinal number 20, occurring after nineteen and before twenty-one.
The numbers twenty (20) to twenty-nine (29).
A banknote with a denomination of 20.

twenty.ety: From Middle English twenty, twenti, from Old English twēntiġ (“twenty”, literally “two tens”), from Proto-Germanic *twaintigiwiz, *twai tigiwiz, an old compound of *twain- (“two”) + *-tigaz (“group of ten”), equivalent to two + -ty, or twain + -ty. Cognate with Scots twenty, tuenty (“twenty”), West Frisian tweintich (“twenty”), Dutch twintig (“twenty”), German zwanzig (“twenty”), Danish tyve.

ex.en: Can I call you back in twenty minutes?
ex.ja: ２０分後に電話を掛け直してもいいですか。

ex.en: I'll be back in twenty minutes or so.
ex.ja: ２０分かそこらで戻ります。

ex.en: Twenty miles is a long distance to walk.
ex.ja: ２０マイルは、歩くのに長い距離だ。

note.ja: 古英語 twēntig ＝ two + -ty（10）。「2つの10」。

en: Of, pertaining to, characteristic of, or happening or located in, a city or town; of, pertaining to, or characteristic of life in such a …
Living in a city or town.

urban.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *werbʰ-der.
Proto-Italic *worβis?

en: Of or relating to an institution; institutional.

ex.ja: 日本の企業業績は改善した。

ex.ja: 企業倒産は先月も高水準に推移した。

ex.ja: 私たちは会議でこのテーマについて討論するだろう。

note.ja: 古フランス語 debatre（打ち合う）から。de + battre（打つ）。「言葉で打ち合う」→「討論」。battle と同じ。

ex.en: Our lives are determined by our environment.
ex.ja: 我々の生活は環境によって決定される。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ termin（境界）。境界をはっきり定める →「決定する・決心する」。

en: An original or official paper used as the basis, proof, or support of anything else, including any writing, book, or other instrument con…
